title: BCLP partners with Legora after thorough and extensive pilot
author: Legora

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source supports the platform-led adoption proposition: BCLP tested Legora in selected workflows before committing to firmwide rollout, then planned continued collaboration with Legora’s engineers to integrate it further. Its unquantified performance claims and prospective client benefits also fit the cluster’s distinction between deployment and demonstrated outcomes.
qs: BCLP’s lawyers tested the platform in a range of workflows, including document review, due diligence, and legal drafting.
The Innovation Team, in collaboration with the firm’s Innovation Champions, will now focus on working closely with Legora’s engineers to integrate the tool further into BCLP’s legal workflows.

kp.k: BCLP tested Legora with over 100 lawyers
kp.d: BCLP’s adoption followed a pilot lasting several months, involving over 100 lawyers across multiple practice areas and jurisdictions. The document characterises the testing as rigorous and reports that participants used Legora for document review, due diligence and legal drafting.
qs: After a successful pilot that saw rigorous testing by over 100 of its lawyers across multiple practice areas and jurisdictions, international law firm BCLP has now partnered with Legora.
The trial period ran over several months, and Legora was recognised as being unmatched in its capabilities by those taking part.
BCLP’s lawyers tested the platform in a range of workflows, including document review, due diligence, and legal drafting.

kp.k: Pilot reportedly improved efficiency, accuracy and satisfaction
kp.d: Legora reports that pilot feedback was overwhelmingly positive and that the results showed significant improvements in efficiency, accuracy and participating lawyers’ overall satisfaction. These claims are not accompanied by numerical performance measures in the document.
qs: User feedback during the pilot was overwhelmingly positive, and the results demonstrated significant improvements in efficiency, accuracy, and overall satisfaction among the participating lawyers.

Legora’s ability to enable lawyers to work with drastically improved efficiency came to the fore during the trial period - one pilot member described the platform as ‘tremendously useful and irreplaceable when it comes to working with large suites of documents’.

kp.k: BCLP plans firmwide rollout and workflow integration
kp.d: Following the pilot, BCLP partnered with Legora for a firmwide rollout intended to streamline operations and improve efficiency. BCLP’s Innovation Team and Innovation Champions will work with Legora’s engineers to integrate the platform more deeply into legal workflows.
qs: The platform will be rolled out across the firm to streamline operational processes and improve efficiency.
The Innovation Team, in collaboration with the firm’s Innovation Champions, will now focus on working closely with Legora’s engineers to integrate the tool further into BCLP’s legal workflows.

kp.k: BCLP expects AI to enhance legal service delivery
kp.d: BCLP’s Innovation Team identified multiple opportunities for Legora to enhance service delivery and support favourable client outcomes. David Boulds presents the partnership as part of a broader effort to use AI for transformational change in legal practice.
qs: Following an in-depth review, BCLP’s Innovation Team has identified numerous opportunities where Legora can make a real difference in enhancing service delivery and ensuring favourable outcomes for the firm’s clients.

Our partnership with Legora signifies a substantial step forward in the use of AI technology at the firm. We are building on our deep experience in the application of AI to deliver real transformational change to our practice of law.

kp.k: Efficiency may redirect lawyers toward valued advisory work
kp.d: The document predicts that using Legora will allow BCLP lawyers to devote greater attention to business-critical legal advice valued by clients, framing AI as augmenting lawyers by reducing effort devoted to operational or document-intensive work.
qs: Using Legora, BCLP’s lawyers will be able to have a greater focus on providing the business-critical legal advisory services that the firm’s clients truly value.

kp.k: Pilot user claimed unmatched document-analysis sophistication
kp.d: A pilot participant quoted by Legora described the platform as irreplaceable for large document sets and asserted that no comparable tool offered the same document-reading and analysis sophistication. This is an individual user assessment reported in the vendor’s newsroom account.
qs: Legora’s unparalleled capabilities and quality were also recognised during the trial period, with the pilot user also stating that ‘there is no other comparable tool that is capable of reading and analysing documents with that level of sophistication’.

kp.k: BCLP links adoption to modernisation and client service
kp.d: BCLP frames the partnership as an investment in digital modernisation, efficiency and improved client service. Its chief information officer says the technology should provide teams with better tools and insights for addressing client needs in a more complex legal environment.
qs: BCLP is committed to business modernisation, leveraging technology and investing in digital solutions to enhance efficiency and deliver superior client service.
This partnership will equip our teams with superior tools and insights, enabling us to better address our clients' needs in an increasingly complex legal landscape.
Our objective is to remain at the forefront of legal technology, and this partnership underscores our commitment to this goal.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Legora’s newsroom reports pilot improvements in lawyers’ efficiency, accuracy and satisfaction, and predicts that firmwide adoption will improve service delivery and free lawyers to focus on business-critical advice.
pts.d: Team Legora claims that BCLP’s pilot demonstrated improvements in document-related work and that the rollout will streamline operational processes. It reports that BCLP’s Innovation Team identified opportunities to enhance service delivery and client outcomes. An unnamed pilot participant describes Legora as particularly useful for large document collections and claims its analytical sophistication is unmatched by comparable tools. BCLP Global Director of Innovation David Boulds frames the partnership as building on existing AI experience to transform legal practice. BCLP Global Chief Information Officer Dan Surowiec predicts that the tools and insights will enable teams to better address client needs. These are claims about augmenting lawyers’ work; the source does not predict job losses, autonomous legal service delivery or changes to fees.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The offered evidence consists of a multi-month internal pilot involving over 100 lawyers, user feedback, an Innovation Team review and statements from firm leaders and Legora’s CEO.
pts.d: The vendor-authored announcement describes testing across multiple practice areas and jurisdictions in document review, due diligence and legal drafting. It supports the improvement claims with qualitative accounts of pilot results and participant testimony, and the prospective service-delivery benefits with the Innovation Team’s review and executive statements. It provides no numerical efficiency or accuracy results, measurement definitions, comparison protocol, named competing tools or independently reported evaluation. The claim of unmatched capability is attributed to pilot participants rather than supported by a disclosed comparative benchmark. Legora CEO Max Junestrand characterises the feedback as exceptional and anticipates further product improvements.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The source distinguishes reported gains during a completed multi-month pilot from anticipated benefits of a forthcoming firmwide rollout and further workflow integration.
pts.d: Published on August 7, 2025, the announcement says the partnership follows several months of testing. Efficiency, accuracy and satisfaction gains are presented as already observed among pilot participants. Broader operational and client-service benefits are prospective, associated with rolling the platform out across BCLP and integrating it further into legal workflows through collaboration between the firm’s Innovation Team, Innovation Champions and Legora engineers. No rollout completion date, quantified future target or timetable for the promised future innovations is specified.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The principal affected groups are BCLP’s lawyers, its innovation and implementation teams, and its clients.
pts.d: The reported pilot benefits concern over 100 lawyers at an international law firm across multiple practice areas and jurisdictions, with particular relevance to document-intensive workflows. The planned rollout extends the intended efficiency and advisory-focus benefits across the firm. BCLP’s Innovation Team and Innovation Champions, together with Legora engineers, are responsible for further integration. Clients are presented as indirect beneficiaries through greater attention to business-critical advice, better responsiveness to their needs and anticipated improvements in service and outcomes. Junestrand also expresses a broader ambition to empower legal professionals globally, but the specific experience reported is BCLP’s pilot.
